chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi from Jamil from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He begins in Mina with slaughtering before shaving (the head), and in the 'Aqiqah with shaving before slaughting. If he does the opposite of that out of forgetfulness, there is no penalty upon him. He narrated that.

key_terms.الْعَقِيقَةِ: 'Aqiqah, the ritual sacrifice performed on the occasion of a child's birth
key_terms.فَلَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is no penalty/obligation upon him
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca central to Hajj rituals

ai.seo_question: What is the correct order of slaughtering and shaving during Hajj and 'Aqiqah?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinct procedural orders for Hajj and 'Aqiqah, establishing that while Hajj requires slaughter before shaving (al-halq), 'Aqiqah mandates shaving before slaughter. This distinction highlights the specific jurisprudential nuances (fiqh) within Shia tradition regarding ritual purity and sacrifice, ensuring that the physical act of shaving is not conflated with the act of slaughter in different contexts. The ruling on forgetfulness (nisyan) underscores the principle of ease in worship, where unintentional deviation does not incur penalty.
